meta.rule: Only what you have proven you own and confirmed is scanned.

rule: Scanning your external surface is active scanning, so Vedette sets two conditions. First, you prove ownership of each target: a domain with a DNS TXT record; a public IP you type in with a token file served on it or a reverse DNS name under one of your proved domains; a public IP the box finds as its own egress address is proved by that detection. Every proof is looked for again right before every scan and by the box itself before it runs out; each time it is found it holds for 90 days more. A check that does not find it is shown as a warning and does not stop scans until those 90 days have passed. Second, an administrator with two-step sign-in confirms that your company owns it and that the scan is authorized: the first Scan now of a target records that confirmation, with the exact sentence shown beside the button. Until then the button stays locked for everyone else. Every verification and scan is written to the audit log.

risky.voip: Phone systems (SIP) are scanned all day for toll fraud: attackers guess extension passwords and make paid calls on your bill.
risky.remote: Remote access is the most attacked way in: attackers guess passwords and use known flaws to log in.
risky.files: File sharing should never face the Internet: ransomware gangs scan for it.
risky.database: Databases should never face the Internet: they are scanned for weak or missing passwords to steal or wipe the data.
risky.control: This service controls the device or the containers on it: whoever reaches it can take the device over.
risky.camera: Camera recorders are taken over in bulk for botnets, often with factory passwords.

Select Verify again to check now.

help.how: The box asks three public "what is my IP" services over HTTPS: checkip.amazonaws.com (AWS), icanhazip.com (Cloudflare) and ifconfig.me/ip (Google Cloud). It accepts an IP only when at least two of them return the same one, so one wrong answer is not enough. A full check does this in 5 rounds on new connections (15 requests), so several IPs behind a load balancer all show up. The first check after install, Detect now and Verify again are full checks. The automatic checks after that ask each service once (3 requests).
help.result: Each IP the box sees is added or renewed for 90 days from that moment. An IP expires only when the box has not seen it for 90 days; until then it stays scannable, even while the box goes out through another IP.
help.why: You cannot type an IP. Only an address the box really uses proves it belongs to your network, so nobody can verify someone else's address.
help.refuse: Private, reserved and shared carrier (CGNAT, 100.64.0.0/10) addresses are refused, because scanning them could hit other people.
help.limit: Detect now, Verify again and the DNS Check of a domain share 10 attempts per hour. Automatic checks do not use them: they can run as often as every minute, and a full check runs at most once an hour by itself. Every change is written to the audit log.

greenbone.title: Optional deep scan: OpenVAS
greenbone.description: Adds an OpenVAS scan to each deep scan of this box's public IP. Off by default.
greenbone.descriptionInfo: OpenVAS (Greenbone Community Edition, free, with the Greenbone Community Feed; not the paid Greenbone Enterprise) is an open-source vulnerability scanner that runs as its own containers next to Vedette. When it is on, each scan of the box's own verified public IP whose testing terms are accepted ends with an OpenVAS scan of that IP.

stateText.off: OpenVAS is off. Scans do not use it.
stateText.ready: OpenVAS is ready. The next scan of an IP of this box uses it.

greenbone.loading: OpenVAS is loading its vulnerability tests.
greenbone.what: It looks at your public IP from outside without logging in, with the OpenVAS "Full and fast" tests, only once that IP's testing terms are accepted (Ownership tab): every non-disruptive check, active ones included, with safe checks on; with the disruptive checks ticked, brute force, default accounts, denial of service and generic web application scanning too, with safe checks off (this can run up to the time cap).
greenbone.apart: Its results are shown in their own section of each scan. They never replace or hide what Vedette found by version, and finding nothing is not proof that nothing is affected.
greenbone.weekly: While it is on, Vedette updates the OpenVAS feed once a week, never during a scan, and only with 60 GB free.
greenbone.offKeeps: Turning it off stops its containers and keeps its images and data, so turning it on again does not download them again.
greenbone.feedTestsInfo: The date of the Greenbone Community Feed that OpenVAS reports it has loaded (version {{version}}). The feed comes with the first load when OpenVAS is turned on; after that Vedette updates it once a week.
greenbone.feedFirstDone: First full feed load done; the weekly update has not run yet
greenbone.feedFirstDoneAt: First full feed load done (OpenVAS turned on {{time}}); the weekly update has not run yet
greenbone.needs: Needs about 50 GB of disk. Turning it on the first time takes 1 to 3 hours.
greenbone.needsInfo: The box must have at least 6 GB of memory (under 8 GB, also 2 GB of swap) and 60 GB free.
greenbone.swapNote: The first feed load uses swap on a box under 8 GB.
greenbone.swapNoteInfo: On a 7 GB box it used about 2 GB of swap.
greenbone.offWaiting: Stopping the OpenVAS containers… this can take a few minutes.
greenbone.heldOn: It is still turned on from before: turn it off to stop its containers. Its data is kept.
greenbone.toastOn: OpenVAS is starting. The first time takes 1 to 3 hours; it shows Ready when it is done.
greenbone.waitTitle: OpenVAS takes 1 to 3 hours to start the first time
greenbone.waitText: It downloads about 9 GB and loads tens of thousands of vulnerability tests. Please be patient: you can leave this page, and it shows Ready when it is done.
greenbone.toastOff: OpenVAS is off. Its data is kept.
